gaps.sentence: It's ___ eight o'clock news — hurry up!
gaps.explanation: 'The eight o'clock news' — a specific, known programme.

gaps.sentence: ___ good news is that sales are up by twenty per cent.
gaps.explanation: 'News' is uncountable but takes 'the' when specified: the good news is… 'Sales' here is general, so no article.

gaps.sentence: We go to ___ cinema about once a month.
gaps.explanation: 'Go to the cinema/theatre' is a fixed phrase with 'the'.

gaps.sentence: It's ___ one-way street, so you can't turn left here.
gaps.explanation: 'One' starts with /w/, a consonant sound, so 'a one-way street'.

gaps.sentence: They say ___ apple a day keeps the doctor away.
gaps.explanation: 'An apple a day…' — 'an' before the vowel sound, 'a' before 'day'.
'MA' is pronounced /em/, starting with a vowel sound, so 'an MA'.

gaps.sentence: ___ Smith family have lived in this street since 1990.
gaps.explanation: 'The Smith family' — the whole family takes 'the'.

gaps.sentence: ___ Alps attract skiers from all over the world.
gaps.explanation: Mountain ranges take 'the' (the Alps), but single peaks take no article (Everest).
